findings.claim: The commit deletes the e2e test 'find with the inspector closed in a stacked row restores the canvas scroll' from inspector-responsive-layout-desktop.spec.ts, a file that is not in the touch-point list and covers the stacked inspector, which the spec declares unchanged.
findings.impact: The regression check that find-close restores canvas scroll in the stacked inspector form is gone. A later break of that behaviour passes the suite silently. The commit gives no reason for the removal in the spec or the review record.
findings.evidence: Diff hunk 'diff --git a/frontend/e2e-components/inspector-responsive-layout-desktop.spec.ts' '@@ -611,48 +611,6 @@' removes the whole test. Grep for 'restores the canvas scroll' in frontend/ now returns no match. The spec's '## Checked, no action' lists the stacked inspector as 'Not this change' and no invariant I-line covers it.
findings.repro: not_reproduced: static reading only; no test run was possible. The removal is visible in the diff.

bucket_proposal.reason: No declared invariant covers the stacked-inspector find scroll restore, so this breaks no I-line. It is an unplanned removal of coverage that reads wrong for a feature the spec says is unchanged.

findings.proposed_fix: Restore the test, or record in the spec why it is removed and which test replaces its coverage.

findings.claim: player-workbench-desktop.spec.ts has an existing SPEC-CORE-085 I5 test rewritten from 'keeps 18rem and the page scrolls' to 'shrinks below 18rem and does not scroll'. The file is not in the touch-point list; the list only anticipates tests found by grepping WORKBENCH_MIN_REM.
findings.impact: The old floor assertion, which encoded the behaviour being removed, is replaced in place under a new SPEC-CORE-106 name. A reader of the 085 test history cannot tell that the 085 floor was dropped by an edit to that test.
findings.evidence: Diff hunk 'frontend/e2e-components/player-workbench-desktop.spec.ts' '@@ -195,7 +195,7 @@' changes the test title to 'SPEC-CORE-106 I1 ...' and replaces the PANEL_FLOOR and scrolls==true expectations with toBeLessThan(PANEL_FLOOR) and scrolls==false. Spec Revises section: SPEC-CORE-085 I5 is revised, so the edit matches the revision.

bucket_proposal.reason: The edit follows the revised invariant text (SPEC-CORE-085 I5 revised; SPEC-CORE-106 I1). It is an untracked touch point, and it reads as a silent rename of a 085 test. No I-line is broken by the test edit itself.

findings.proposed_fix: Record this file in the touch-point list, or keep the 085 test name and add the 106 test beside it.

findings.claim: useCompanionMetrics adds a MutationObserver with childList and subtree over the whole document (scope = document when no mini player), and a beside-form exception in rowBlockPx, neither of which the spec's rowBlock formula or touch-point description includes.
findings.impact: Every DOM insertion or removal anywhere on the canonical page runs a querySelector on the workbench row, which costs time on busy pages. The beside exception returns rowBlock 0 when data-row-beside is on. That is not visible today, because the beside state needs a panel shown and the cap is then half of H, but it is a silent divergence from the spec's formula in §3.
findings.evidence: frontend/src/components/FileDetail/hooks/useCompanionMetrics.ts: rowBlockPx() returns 0 when row.closest('[data-row-beside="on"]'); the new mutationObserver.observe(scope, { childList: true, subtree: true }) in the effect. Spec §3 defines rowBlock = offsetHeight + 2rem, with 0 only when no row is drawn. The MutationObserver is not mentioned in the spec's touch point for this file.
findings.repro: not_reproduced. The MutationObserver is not covered by any jsdom test. The beside case is not reached with a panel shown and the cap at half H.

bucket_proposal.reason: No I-line is broken: under the current cap rules the beside zero has no visible effect, and the observer cost is not a stated invariant. Both diverge from the spec's written formula and mechanism, so the behaviour is surprising to a reader.

findings.proposed_fix: Either document the beside exception and the document-wide observer in the spec, or narrow the observer to the row's parent and use the same check for beside as the spec's formula.

findings.claim: The spec's planned touch points ShellLayout.tsx (row element held in state) and Workbench.tsx (rowRef callback ref) are absent from the diff; the implementation finds the row with querySelector('.media-detail-workbench-row') on every measure.
findings.impact: Not a user-visible defect on its own, because the MutationObserver covers mount and unmount. But the declared touch-point list does not match the code, so a reviewer checking the diff against the spec's touch points finds a missing planned change and an unplanned mechanism.
findings.evidence: frontend/src/components/FileDetail/ShellLayout.tsx is unchanged in the diff (no useState for the row element, no rowRef prop passed to the hook). frontend/src/components/FileDetail/workbench/Workbench.tsx has no rowRef; the row is at line 95 as '<div className="media-detail-workbench-row">' with no ref. The spec's 'Touch points' lists both files.

bucket_proposal.reason: The code is authoritative and the spec's mechanism is not a checked contract. The mismatch is only a discrepancy with the declared touch-point list, and no I-line depends on how the row is found.

findings.proposed_fix: Update the spec's touch-point list and §3 to describe the querySelector and MutationObserver approach, or switch to the rowRef design as written.

findings.claim: The updated jsdom expectations in FileDetailCanvas.test.tsx change only by the removed 48px peek (508→556, 632→680, 402→450), so no jsdom test exercises the rowBlock subtraction.
findings.impact: A regression that drops or doubles rowBlock would pass the unit suite. Only the e2e file, which cannot run here, measures the row subtraction in a real browser.
findings.evidence: frontend/src/components/FileDetail/__tests__/FileDetailCanvas.test.tsx lines 213, 219, 278, 288: the new values equal the old values plus 48 exactly. The test stubs getBoundingClientRect and offsetHeight is 0 in jsdom, so a row present in this test would give rowBlock 32px and a different value. The +48 result shows no row was rendered.
findings.repro: not_reproduced: static reading. Mutation to try: set rowBlockPx to return 0 always; the jsdom suite should still pass.

bucket_proposal.reason: The test values are internally consistent, so no I-line is broken. The gap is in what the suite can catch, not in the code's behaviour.

findings.proposed_fix: Add a jsdom case that renders the workbench row with a stubbed offsetHeight and asserts the player budget is reduced by offsetHeight plus 2rem.

findings.claim: mediaDetailTheaterCss.test.ts is edited (the canonical host min-height assertion becomes a height assertion plus a not-min-height check). The touch-point list keeps this file only for the collection test and does not list the canonical assertion as an expected change.
findings.impact: The regex '[^-]height:' also matches any non-min height rule in the stylesheet, so the check is looser than its name. A future change to a different height rule could satisfy it without the host being fixed.
findings.evidence: Diff hunk 'frontend/src/app/__tests__/mediaDetailTheaterCss.test.ts' '@@ -48,9 +48,8 @@': the expectation becomes /[^-]height:\s*var\(--rail-avail,\s*100dvh\);/ with a separate not.toMatch(/min-height/). The host block is extracted from globals.css, so the match is on the extracted block only.

bucket_proposal.reason: The edit is necessary for the spec's change and matches its intent. The only issue is the loose regex, which reads wrong but breaks no I-line.

findings.proposed_fix: Anchor the regex to the host block's own selector, or assert the exact declaration and drop the loose match.

specification_compliance: Unplanned places the diff reaches outside the touch-point list: (1) frontend/e2e-components/inspector-responsive-layout-desktop.spec.ts, a deleted stacked-inspector test; (2) frontend/e2e-components/player-workbench-desktop.spec.ts, an existing 085 I5 test rewritten; (3) frontend/src/app/__tests__/mediaDetailTheaterCss.test.ts, the canonical host assertion changed; (4) frontend/e2e-components/projects.ts and spec-viewport.spec.ts, the new spec's registration, which is implicit to the new e2e file and is not reported as unplanned; (5) inside the listed useCompanionMetrics.ts, the beside exception and the document-wide MutationObserver, which the spec's rowBlock formula does not describe.
Planned touch points not reached by the diff: ShellLayout.tsx and Workbench.tsx (rowRef). The row is found with querySelector instead.
globals.css change is limited to the host rule; data-workbench is set only from workbenchWide && shownPanels.length > 0 (ShellLayout.tsx:458), so the height rule applies only with a panel shown.
WORKBENCH_MIN_REM has no remaining references under frontend/ (grep shows none); layoutSizes.ts deletion is complete.
potential_unspecified_behavior: The beside exception in rowBlockPx returns 0 when data-row-beside is on. The spec's rowBlock formula has no such case. It is invisible today, because beside requires a panel shown and the cap is then half of H.

The MutationObserver watches childList only. A change to data-row-beside alone does not trigger measure(); it relies on the ResizeObserver on the row. If the row keeps the same height across a beside toggle, rowBlock can be stale. Not verified.
With no miniPlayerRoot the scope is document, so the observer runs on every DOM insertion or removal in the page.
regression_risks: Removing the stacked find test leaves the find-close scroll restore in the stacked form without any check.
The subtree MutationObserver on document adds per-mutation querySelector cost on the canonical page.
FileDetailCanvas expectations were changed to values that assume no row; a later change that renders the row in those tests would fail them for a reason unrelated to the test intent.
test_coverage: The jsdom suite does not exercise rowBlock (its expected values equal the old values plus 48px), so the subtraction and the beside exception are untested there.
The new e2e file workbench-no-page-scroll-desktop.spec.ts measures the live budget, the row and the scroll at several H values. It was not run here.
The stacked find-restore e2e test was removed, so that behaviour has no test in the diff.
not_verified: No test was run and no browser measurement was made; I had only Read, Glob and Grep.
I did not read the full e2e-components fixtures or the e2e-layout static CSS fixtures, so I did not check whether they reference the removed min-height rule.
I did not check the complete diff for ShellLayout.tsx (unchanged in the diff) against any other consumer of the metrics hook beyond the grep for the row class.
I did not verify whether the stacked find test's removal hides a real regression, because the test could not be run.
